label: History
value: Mr. Allan brought his young bride to Avonlea five years before the current time.
unit: Having brought his young bride to Avonlea five years prior, Mr. Allan served as the town's minister. During a social visit to Green Gables early in his tenure, he and his wife attended a tea prepared by Anne, where Mrs. Allan accidentally sampled a layer cake flavored with anodyne liniment. Following the sudden death of Matthew Cuthbert, Mr. Allan provided spiritual support and comfort to Anne as she grieved. His eventual departure from Avonlea was noted by the local community as Anne completed her tenure as the town's schoolteacher.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was taken in at Green Gables.
unit: Anne Shirley, an adopted orphan without family, was taken in at Green Gables after being sent by mistake instead of a boy, though Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert soon decided to keep and raise her. Shortly after arriving, she vowed eternal friendship with Diana Barry in the garden at Orchard Slope. Her early years at Green Gables were marked by dramatic misadventures, including accidentally getting Diana drunk on currant wine, falling from a roof and breaking her ankle on a dare, and being forced to cut her hair short after trying to dye her red hair black with peddler's dye. Despite these mishaps, she proved her resourcefulness by saving Diana's baby sister from croup, earned the forgiveness of local adults like Mrs. Barry and Miss Josephine Barry, and excelled academically by joining Miss Stacy's advanced class to prepare for Queen's Academy. Anne later became a beloved local teacher and led the Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside Gilbert Blythe, though she made notable mistakes like selling her neighbor's cow by accident and accidentally staining her nose red with rug dye. She attended Redmond College with her friends, during which time she rejected marriage proposals from both Gilbert Blythe and wealthy Roy Gardner while pursuing her writing ambitions. After graduating and continuing her career as a schoolteacher, she eventually reconciled her feelings for Gilbert. With her college years behind her, Anne completed her teaching duties and prepared to marry Gilbert before relocating to Four Winds Harbor.

Her early years at Green Gables were marked by dramatic misadventures, including accidentally getting Diana drunk on currant wine, falling from a roof and breaking her ankle on a dare, and being forced to cut her hair short after trying to dye her red hair black with peddler's dye. Despite these mishaps, she proved her resourcefulness by saving Diana's baby sister from croup, earned the forgiveness of local adults like Mrs. Barry and Miss Josephine Barry, and excelled academically by joining Miss Stacy's advanced class to prepare for Queen's Academy. Anne later became a beloved local teacher and led the Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside Gilbert Blythe, though she made notable mistakes like selling her neighbor's cow by accident and accidentally staining her nose red with rug dye. She attended Redmond College with her friends, during which time she rejected marriage proposals from both Gilbert Blythe and wealthy Roy Gardner while pursuing her writing ambitions. After graduating and continuing her career as a schoolteacher, she eventually reconciled her feelings for Gilbert. With her college years behind her, Anne completed her teaching duties and prepared to marry Gilbert before relocating to Four Winds Harbor.

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’ll fold them nicely tonight. They always made us do that at the asylum. Half the time, though, I’d forget, I’d be in such a hurry to get into bed nice and quiet and imagine things."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’d do anything to oblige you. But you’ll have to tell me what to say for this once. After I get into bed I’ll imagine out a real nice prayer to say always. I believe that it will be quite interesting, now that I come to think of it."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "But I’d be ever so much gratefuller if—if you’d made just one of them with puffed sleeves. Puffed sleeves are so fashionable now. It would give me such a thrill, Marilla, just to wear a dress with puffed sleeves."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’ll just eat one tonight, Marilla. And I can give Diana half of them, can’t I? The other half will taste twice as sweet to me if I give some to her. It’s delightful to think I have something to give her."

label: History
value: Anne was born an orphan in Nova Scotia.
unit: An orphan born in Nova Scotia and raised outside Prince Edward Island, Anne was brought to Green Gables by Matthew Cuthbert fourteen years prior to her marriage. Admitted to stay after an initial mix-up, she was brought up by Marilla Cuthbert and established herself in Avonlea by founding the Village Improvement Society and earning the entrance tied-first score for Queen's Academy. During her school years, she survived a drowning attempt on a pond when Gilbert Blythe rescued her, though she maintained a long academic rivalry with him. Anne later attended Redmond College, where she declined a proposal from Billy Andrews via Jane and refused a diamond engagement ring, ultimately accepting a circlet of pearls when she became engaged to Gilbert. Following their wedding, Anne moved with Gilbert to Four Winds Harbor, where she suffered the tragic loss of her firstborn daughter Joyce shortly after birth before later giving birth to a healthy son, James Matthew. In Four Winds, she formed deep friendships with Captain Jim and Leslie Moore, assisting in the events surrounding Captain Jim's life-book and Leslie's freedom from a mistaken marriage. After Captain Jim peacefully passed away, Anne and Gilbert packed up their initial house of dreams and departed for a larger home in the Glen St. Mary area.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina came to live at Patty's Place
unit: Aunt Jamesina came to live at Patty's Place to act as housekeeper for Stella Maynard, Anne Shirley, and Priscilla Grant during their college years. She brought her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and quickly established a comfortable, cheerful household routine with the girls, freely sharing her relaxed views on chaperoning and stories about her past suitors. Throughout their time together, she provided a warm domestic presence, chatting with the young women about their studies, romantic entanglements, and visitors, while witnessing major events such as Phil Gordon's engagement and Anne's suitors. Following the end of their college years and the group's departure from Patty's Place, Aunt Jamesina traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field, overcoming her personal horror of snakes to do so.

Following the end of their college years and the group's departure from Patty's Place, Aunt Jamesina traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field, overcoming her personal horror of snakes to do so.

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "She couldn’t take Joseph with her so she begged me to take him. I really couldn’t refuse. He’s a beautiful cat—that is, his disposition is beautiful. She called him Joseph because his coat is of many colors."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Kittens have to be drowned, I admit, or the world would be overrun. But no decent, grown-up cat should be done to death—unless he sucks eggs."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Well, I hope so, Anne. I do hope so, because I love her. But I can’t understand her—she beats me. She isn’t like any of the girls I ever knew, or any of the girls I was myself."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Yes, in my soul. But I’ll admit my legs aren’t as young as yours. You go and get some fresh air, Anne. You look pale lately."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Anybody is liable to rheumatism in her legs, Anne. It’s only old people who should have rheumatism in their souls, though. Thank goodness, I never have. When you get rheumatism in your soul you might as well go and pick out your coffin."

label: History
value: Aunt Josephine is the great-aunt of Diana Barry.
unit: Aunt Josephine was the wealthy great-aunt of Diana Barry who lived at Beechwood in Charlottetown. During a visit to Orchard Slope, she was infuriated when Anne Shirley and Diana accidentally jumped on top of her in the spare-room bed, but she was so won over by Anne's brave, sincere apology that she decided to stay in Avonlea and became firm friends with her. She later sent Anne kid slippers for Christmas and hosted Anne and Diana at her estate for the Exhibition in Charlottetown. After enduring a dreadful illness that lasted over a year, Aunt Josephine passed away, leaving Anne a legacy of one thousand dollars in her will to secure her college education.

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: “I’m afraid my imagination is a little rusty—it’s so long since I used it,” she said. “I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself.”

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: “I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,” she said frankly. “She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity.”

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: "Mercy, child, how you have grown! You’re taller than I am, I declare. And you’re ever so much better-looking than you used to be, too. But I dare say you know that without being told."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth was a young maid.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth was a young maid who worked for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge when she was fourteen years old. She often entertained visiting guests alongside her employer, hosting pretend tea parties in the garden. Concerned by Miss Lavendar's frequent melancholy, Charlotta confided her worries to Anne Shirley, leading Anne to promise to visit more often. She later helped Anne prepare the house for Stephen Irving's return, anxiously waiting in the kitchen until she witnessed the couple's happy reconciliation. Charlotta subsequently assisted with the wedding preparations at Echo Lodge, eventually marrying a good-tempered bricklayer named Tom. Years later, she traveled back to Avonlea to attend Anne's wedding to Gilbert Blythe at Green Gables.

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "it’s plain to be seen you and Miss Lavendar have got a secret and I think, begging your pardon if I’m too forward, Miss Shirley, ma’am, that it’s real mean not to tell me when we’ve all been such chums."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "I peeked from the kitchen window . . . and he’s awful handsome . . . and just the right age for Miss Lavendar. And oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, do you think it would be much harm to listen at the door?"

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "But I’m sure I shan’t sleep a blessed wink, Miss Shirley, ma’am, for fear that something’ll go wrong at the last minute . . . the cream won’t whip . . . or Mr. Irving’ll have a stroke and not be able to come."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "but there’s so much to do yet . . . and oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "Yes, ma’am. Come in, ma’am. I’ll tell Miss Lavendar you’re here, ma’am. She’s upstairs, ma’am."

label: History
value: Miss Cornelia Bryant is a local resident.
unit: Miss Cornelia Bryant, a candid local resident with strong opinions on men, ministers, and neighbors, introduced herself to Anne Blythe by calling at her home shortly after Anne and Gilbert settled in Four Winds Harbor. She frequented the house to share local news, including the tragic history of their neighbor Leslie Moore, whom she encouraged Anne to befriend. Cornelia frequently joined the Blythes and Captain Jim for gatherings, engaging in spirited debates over holiday dinners and casual visits. Though she often expressed fierce opinions, such as her strong disapproval when Gilbert proposed a medical operation to cure Dick Moore, she maintained close ties with the household. After the operation ultimately revealed that the man was not Dick Moore, Cornelia arrived at Anne's in total shock to discuss Leslie's sudden freedom. She remained a fixture in the community through seasonal celebrations, political discussions, and personal milestones, including the birth of Anne's son. Cornelia eventually surprised her friends by announcing her intention to marry Marshall Elliott, putting aside her long-held, sharp criticisms of men.

label: History
value: Davy Keith moved to Green Gables
unit: Davy Keith moved to Green Gables as a rowdy orphan alongside his twin sister, Dora, to live under the care of Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley. During his early months at Green Gables, Davy frequently caused chaos by dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, ruining Dora's dress, and locking his sister in a toolhouse. He repeatedly struggled with lying and skipping his prayers, but Anne consistently counseled him through his confessions and guilt. Despite misbehaving further by spoiling dinner party pies during a visit from a famous author, Davy retained a permanent home at Green Gables after money from his late father's brother provided for the twins' upkeep. Over the years, Davy grew attached to Anne, confiding his jealousies, theological confusions, and moral dilemmas to her, including a night when he confessed to skipping Sunday School to go fishing. As Anne attended college, Davy welcomed her back during her holiday visits, sharing chatter about his schoolwork, lost teeth, and childhood musings. He was present with his family when Anne married Gilbert Blythe in the Green Gables orchard, and he later traveled from Avonlea to spend Christmas with the newly married couple at their home in Four Winds.

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "I just did it for fun. Things have been so awful quiet here for so long that I thought it would be fun to give you folks a big scare. It was, too."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I never will, now that I know it’s bad,” asseverated Davy between sobs. “If you ever catch me telling a whopper again you can . . .” Davy groped mentally for a suitable penance . . . “you can skin me alive, Anne.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Why?” queried Davy, settling comfortably down and looking up with a tearstained, investigating face. “Why ain’t whopper as good as falsehood? I want to know. It’s just as big a word.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Then,” said Davy decidedly, “Marilla is bad, for she tells them. And she’s worse’n me, for I didn’t know it was wrong but she does.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I’ll do it,” volunteered Davy, “if Marilla’ll hold them by the legs, ’cause I guess it’d take both my hands to manage the axe. It’s awful jolly fun to see them hopping about after their heads are cut off.”

Though Diana did not join the advanced Queen's Entrance class alongside Anne, she continued to share adventures with her, including collecting donations for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and helping Anne recover from a facial dye mishap to successfully host famous guest Mrs. Morgan.

label: History
value: Diana was named by a schoolmaster.
unit: Named by a schoolmaster who was boarding at her home when she was born, Diana spent her childhood at Orchard Slope. As a girl, she learned a fancy crochet stitch from her aunt in Carmody, imagined ghosts in the Haunted Wood, helped form a schoolgirl story club, named local landmarks alongside Anne Shirley, and vowed eternal friendship with Anne in the garden at Orchard Slope. When Mrs. Barry mistakenly believed Anne had deliberately gotten Diana drunk, Diana was forbidden from playing with her, leading to a tearful farewell until Anne saved Minnie May's life and restored their bond. Together, the two friends shared many adventures, including accidentally leaping onto Aunt Josephine in a spare room bed, securing an antique willow-ware platter from Miss Sarah Copp, and discovering Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. As they grew older, Diana was the one who delivered the news of Anne's tie for first place on the Queen's Entrance exams, and she later secretly submitted Anne's short story to a baking powder contest, resulting in a prize win. In time, Diana fell in love with Fred Wright, and Anne helped her prepare for their wedding at Orchard Slope. Four years into her marriage, Diana welcomed a new baby, and she was later present at Green Gables to see Anne marry Gilbert Blythe.

label: Personality
value: Dora is remarkably quiet.
unit: Dora is a remarkably quiet, demure, and well-behaved young girl who comports herself as a model child. Known for her prim and proper demeanor, she remains composed, placid, and dispassionate even in unsettling situations. She is exceptionally neat, careful, faithful, and systematic in all her endeavors, never needing to be told how to perform a task twice. An industrious and helpful individual, her sensible and womanly nature makes her reliable, though her predictable manners can seem monotonous to others. Despite her steady composure, she harbors a distinct fear regarding Mirabel Cotton's deceased uncle.

label: History
value: Dora Keith was brought to live at Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert.
unit: Dora Keith, along with her twin brother Davy, was brought to live at Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert after their mother passed away. Early in her stay, Davy forced her to walk a pigpen fence and pumped water over her, ruining her dress. She was later locked in Mr. Harrison's toolhouse by her brother before being found by Anne Shirley and Mr. Barry. Following the death of her uncle Richard Keith, a trust fund was left that allowed Dora and Davy to stay permanently at Green Gables. As she grew older, Dora was comforted by Anne at school after being frightened by ghost stories. She later gave in to Davy's persuasion to skip Sunday School to go fishing, though Davy eventually confessed the trickery.

label: History
value: The First Mate is an orange cat.
unit: The First Mate was an orange cat who was rescued nine years earlier by Captain Jim after being found starving in a tree, entangled by his ribbon collar. Residing at the Four Winds Point lighthouse, he spent his time keeping Captain Jim company and entertaining visiting guests like Anne, Gilbert, and Leslie during their frequent social gatherings and New Year's celebrations. As Captain Jim neared the end of his life, he poignantly asked Anne to take care of the First Mate after his impending death. Following Captain Jim's peaceful passing in his sleep, the First Mate lost his long-time companion at the lighthouse.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after three years in Alberta, quickly rekindling an intense academic rivalry with Anne Shirley after she smashed a slate over his head for teasing her. Despite her lingering silence, Gilbert secretly harbored feelings for her, saved her from drowning on the pond, and eventually tied with her for first place on the Queen's Entrance examinations. They both attended Queen's Academy, where Gilbert earned the class medal while Anne won a scholarship. Upon returning home, Gilbert surrendered his secured teaching position in Avonlea so Anne could stay at Green Gables following Matthew Cuthbert's death, leading to their reconciliation as friends. While teaching locally, Gilbert helped form the Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside Anne before they both departed to attend Redmond College in Kingsport. At Redmond, he excelled academically, winning High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize, while also captaining the Freshman football team and serving as class president. During their second year, Gilbert proposed to Anne in an orchard, but she rejected him, insisting she only viewed him as a friend. Resigned to her decision, he stepped back and allowed rumors to circulate regarding a potential romance with Christine Stuart, which deeply bothered Anne. After graduating, Gilbert contracted a severe case of typhoid fever back in Avonlea, but his eventual recovery prompted a realization of Anne's true feelings. They walked together to Hester Gray's garden, where Gilbert proposed a second time, and she happily accepted. Following their wedding in the Green Gables orchard, Gilbert and Anne moved to Four Winds Harbor, where he established his medical practice. Their early married life brought tragedy when their firstborn daughter, Joyce, died shortly after birth, though they later welcomed a healthy son named James Matthew.

value: Harrison said: "Well, I’ll tell you what, miss, you must help me eat it. I’ll put the kettle on and we’ll have a cup of tea. How will that do?"

value: Harrison said: "I see you haven’t much confidence in my ability to make tea. You’re wrong . . . I can brew up as good a jorum of tea as you ever drank. But go ahead yourself. Fortunately it rained last Sunday, so there’s plenty of clean dishes."

value: James was raised alongside a brother.

value: Jane Andrews is a plain individual.
unit: Jane Andrews is a plain, placid, and amiable individual known for her unshakeable, steady nature. Highly conscientious and plodding in her efforts, she approaches life pragmatically, aiming in her teaching career to earn her salary fairly, satisfy school trustees, and gain professional recognition. She harbors a desire for wealth and luxury items, such as diamonds, and has expressed a determination to devote her entire life to teaching rather than marrying.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea as a classmate and friend of Anne Shirley. During her schooldays, she joined the local "Story Club" organized by Anne to cultivate their imaginations and write romantic tales. As a young woman pursuing education, she eventually went into teaching. In addition to her own pursuits, she acted as an intermediary for her family, once making a formal marriage proposal on behalf of her shy brother Billy to Anne, which Anne declined. Jane later married a wealthy man, becoming the wife of a millionaire, though her marriage remained a happy one. She eventually returned to visit Avonlea along with her mother and Mrs. Jasper Bell to inspect Anne's wedding trousseau prior to Anne's marriage.

As a young woman pursuing education, she eventually went into teaching. In addition to her own pursuits, she acted as an intermediary for her family, once making a formal marriage proposal on behalf of her shy brother Billy to Anne, which Anne declined. Jane later married a wealthy man, becoming the wife of a millionaire, though her marriage remained a happy one. She eventually returned to visit Avonlea along with her mother and Mrs. Jasper Bell to inspect Anne's wedding trousseau prior to Anne's marriage.

label: Personality
value: Jane is a steady individual.
unit: Jane is a steady, plain, and plodding individual known for her sensible and conscientious nature. She possesses an amiable and placid demeanor, presenting herself as a nice, lady-like, and practical woman who is considerate enough to avoid hurting others' feelings. Though dutiful in her endeavors, she can be strict with her pupils and is noted for being crosser than Anne. Initially motivated to devote her entire life to teaching, earn her salary fairly, please the trustees, and reach the School Inspector's roll of honor without ever marrying, she eventually marries and proves to be exceptionally skilled at cooking.

value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea, joining Anne Shirley's story club as a child and later studying in the Queen's Academy preparation class. After passing the entrance examination for Queen's, she attended school and college alongside Anne and Ruby Gillis. Later, Jane took a job teaching at the Avonlea school. During an autumn walk with Anne, Diana, and Priscilla, Jane explored Hester Gray's garden and enjoyed a spring birthday picnic. Soon after, Jane and her friends attempted to persuade Judson Parker not to rent his fences for patent medicine ads, though Parker initially refused them. Years later, Jane hosted Anne for an overnight visit and delivered a marriage proposal to Anne on behalf of her shy brother, Billy. After Anne rejected the offer, Jane coolly accepted the refusal and noted that Billy would likely marry someone else. Jane eventually resigned from her position at the Avonlea school to go West, stole a march on Anne by getting married first, and wed a millionaire before departing for a honeymoon in Europe.

value: Jane departed for a honeymoon in Europe.
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea, joining Anne Shirley's story club as a child and later studying in the Queen's Academy preparation class. After passing the entrance examination for Queen's, she attended school and college alongside Anne and Ruby Gillis. Later, Jane took a job teaching at the Avonlea school. During an autumn walk with Anne, Diana, and Priscilla, Jane explored Hester Gray's garden and enjoyed a spring birthday picnic. Soon after, Jane and her friends attempted to persuade Judson Parker not to rent his fences for patent medicine ads, though Parker initially refused them. Years later, Jane hosted Anne for an overnight visit and delivered a marriage proposal to Anne on behalf of her shy brother, Billy. After Anne rejected the offer, Jane coolly accepted the refusal and noted that Billy would likely marry someone else. Jane eventually resigned from her position at the Avonlea school to go West, stole a march on Anne by getting married first, and wed a millionaire before departing for a honeymoon in Europe.

label: History
value: Miss Janet Sweet was a resident of Valley Road.
unit: Miss Janet Sweet was a resident of Valley Road who lived at Wayside, where she took in Anne Shirley as a boarder during Anne's time as a local schoolteacher. For twenty years, Janet was courted by her neighbor John Douglas, though he never proposed; on her fortieth birthday, she broke down in tears over the situation and briefly snubbed John following Anne's advice to stand up for herself. After John's overbearing mother passed away, John revealed that a secret oath to his late mother had prevented him from marrying, and he finally proposed to Janet.

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "Oh, she does. She’s told me time and again that she’d love to see John settled before her time comes. She’s always giving him hints—you heard her yourself the other day. I thought I’d ha’ gone through the floor."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "You see, Anne, I’ve always been awful fond of John. He might just as well keep coming as not, for there was never anybody else I’d want, so it didn’t matter."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "No, I guess not. I was afraid to try, anyway, for fear he’d think I meant it and just go. I suppose I’m a poor-spirited creature, but that is how I feel. And I can’t help it."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "I know the road home pretty well alone. I ought to, seeing I’ve been traveling it for forty years. So you needn’t trouble yourself, Mr. Douglas."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "Oh, I’m just as glad you did. When I saw John Douglas making off down that road I just felt as if every little bit of joy and happiness that was left in my life was going with him. It was an awful feeling."

During his time at the Glen, he became the first husband of the bride who lived in the house later occupied by Anne and Gilbert. Decades later, his grandson Owen Ford traveled to the region, drawn by his connection to John Selwyn.

However, after delivering a deeply moving sermon, he earned her profound admiration and caused her to nervously realize that she might be falling in love with him.

label: History
value: Joseph was given to Aunt Jamesina
unit: Joseph was given to Aunt Jamesina by his original owner, a dear friend of hers who was moving to Vancouver and could not take him along. Named Joseph because his multi-colored coat recalled a coat of many colors, he was brought to Patty's Place when Aunt Jamesina moved in as chaperone. Upon arrival, he was repeatedly attacked by the resident stray cat, Rusty, though the two eventually resolved their conflicts and became close friends.

label: History
value: Josie Pye was the last of her family to attend the Avonlea school.
unit: Josie Pye was the last of her family to attend the Avonlea school, where she had once earned first prize for knitted lace at the exhibition. During a party at Diana Barry's house, she challenged Anne Shirley to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, an act that resulted in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Later, Josie was among the group of Avonlea students who attended the local school under Miss Stacy's guidance and eventually pursued higher education at Queen's Academy.

label: History
value: Before her marriage, Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge.
unit: Before her marriage, Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge with her young servant, Charlotta the Fourth, named by her father after lavender because he was so fond of the scent. After accidentally wandering onto her property, Anne Shirley introduced Lavendar to Paul Irving, leading Lavendar to share her quiet sadness and reveal her past broken engagement with Paul's father, Stephen Irving. Anne subsequently helped arrange a reunion between Lavendar and Stephen, leading to their reconciliation, engagement, and a garden wedding at Echo Lodge. Following her marriage, Echo Lodge was closed, though Lavendar eventually hosted visits from Anne and questioned her regarding her complicated relationship with Gilbert Blythe.

label: History
value: Leslie Moore suffered immense hardship in her youth.
unit: Leslie Moore suffered immense hardship in her youth, finding her father after he committed suicide at age fourteen. She managed to complete two years of study in one at Queen's Academy using money inherited from her grandmother, later taking a position as a schoolteacher at the Glen school. At age sixteen, however, she was coerced into marrying Dick Moore to prevent Abner Moore from foreclosing on her mother's farm, though her mother died of pneumonia a year later. Living in Four Winds Harbor, Leslie met Anne Blythe on the harbor shore, and after initial distance caused by her painful history, she slowly warmed to Anne through shared visits, eventually confessing her past envy and forging a deep friendship. She took in writer Owen Ford as a summer boarder, and during his stay, she secretly fell in love with him, tearfully confessing her unrequited feelings to Anne when he departed. When Dr. Gilbert Blythe proposed a brain operation that might restore the memory of the brain-injured man believed to be Dick Moore, Leslie borrowed money from Captain Jim to finance the trip to a Montreal hospital. The operation revealed the man was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, leaving Leslie free from her bond and overjoyed to discover the real Dick had died years prior. After returning home, Leslie reconciled her feelings during a stay at Anne's house and accepted Owen Ford when he returned to confess his love, securing their future together shortly before Captain Jim passed away and Owen purchased Anne and Gilbert's home for their summer vacations.

value: Leslie Moore said: "I knew who YOU were, although I had never seen either of you before. I had heard of the new doctor and his bride who were coming to live in Miss Russell’s little house. I—I hated you that very moment, Anne."

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "She is mistaken—or prejudiced. I think my figure IS better—mother was slight and bent by hard work—but she had the face of an angel. I used just to look up at her in worship. We all worshipped her,—father and Kenneth and I."

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: “Kenneth was my brother,” went on Leslie. “Oh, I can’t tell you how I loved him. And he was cruelly killed. Do you know how?”

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "Anne, I saw his little face as the wheel went over him. He fell on his back. Anne—Anne—I can see it now. I shall always see it. Anne, all I ask of heaven is that that recollection shall be blotted out of my memory. O my God!"

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "I can’t tell you—don’t ask me. I wouldn’t mind your knowing—I wish you did know—but I can’t tell you—I can’t tell anyone. I’ve been such a fool, Anne—and oh, it hurts so terribly to be a fool. There’s nothing so painful in the world."

She later commended Anne's personal growth to Marilla at the end of a school term. Recognizing Anne's plain wardrobe, Mrs. Lynde secretly agreed to sew a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for Matthew Cuthbert to give Anne as a Christmas present. unit: Fifty years before the events at Four Winds Point, Margaret fell asleep in her father's dory and drifted out to sea, becoming Captain Jim's long-lost love. label: Personality
value: Marilla Cuthbert is defined by her rigid conscience.
unit: A woman of narrow experience, Marilla Cuthbert is defined by her rigid conscience, self-contained nature, and sensible, sober demeanor. She exhibits a strict and critical disposition, often stoic and unromantic, though she can occasionally display a sarcastic streak. Deeply repressed, she considers displays of deep emotion unseemly, rarely showing excitement and maintaining a customary calm. Her motivation has centered on drilling Anne into a tranquil uniformity of disposition, though she also held a secret hope for Anne to marry Gilbert Blythe, a prospect that brings her immense happiness. In addition to her strict character, she is known for making three-year-old homemade currant wine and crafting round braided mats. While she detests cats and is prone to headaches, she nonetheless worries significantly about Anne.

value: Marilla Cuthbert grew up as a dark, homely child.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert grew up as a dark, homely child and spent a cramped childhood at Green Gables, where she obeyed orders and remained sensitive about her early looks for fifty years. Having inherited an amethyst brooch from her mother and lived peacefully alongside her neighbor Rachel Lynde for forty-five years, Marilla's quiet routine was altered when she and her brother Matthew set out to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, only to receive a young girl named Anne Shirley instead. Though initially shocked and intent on returning Anne, Marilla was moved to pity after hearing the child's tragic background and agreed to let her stay. As she undertook the task of raising, educating, and disciplining the imaginative girl, Marilla developed a deep love and warmth for Anne, realizing the true extent of her affection when Anne broke her ankle in an accident. Over the passing years, Marilla guided Anne through her school days, managed her home when she took in the orphaned Keith twins after her cousin Mary's death, and opened her house to Rachel Lynde after Rachel was widowed. When failing eyesight threatened to force the sale of Green Gables after Matthew's sudden death, Marilla was spared from losing her home when Anne gave up a college scholarship to stay, teach locally, and live beside her. Marilla later cheered Anne's eventual entry into Redmond College, comforted her through her heartbreak over Gilbert Blythe's near-fatal illness, and happily helped prepare for Anne's marriage to Gilbert in the Green Gables orchard. In her later years, Marilla traveled to Four Winds Harbor to visit Anne, remaining a steadfast source of comfort through the heartbreaking loss of Anne's firstborn daughter and returning later to celebrate the birth of her healthy grandson, James Matthew.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott was known as a noted dancer in his youth.
unit: In his youth, Marshall Elliott was known as a noted dancer, but he later made a public vow to refrain from shaving his face or cutting his hair until the Grits political party came to power. Living near Four Winds, he occasionally gathered at the lighthouse with local residents, joining Anne, Gilbert, Leslie, and Captain Jim to celebrate New Year's Eve with music and dancing around the fire. Following a Liberal victory in a federal election, Marshall finally shaved off his long-held beard, causing Anne to temporarily fail to recognize him when they met shortly before Captain Jim's death.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert was raised by a shy, silent father.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert was raised by a shy, silent father who built a home far away from other people, and Matthew grew up to be the first person to offer love and sympathy to Anne Shirley's starved childhood. When he went to the station expecting to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he was met instead by Anne and decided to bring her to Green Gables to let his sister Marilla handle the mistake. Matthew quietly advocated for keeping Anne and gave her simple delights, such as visiting her room to gently persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Lynde so she could stay, and gifting her a package of chocolate sweets. After Anne completed her studies at Queen's Academy, Matthew spent a tender final evening with her before dying suddenly from the shock of reading about the Abbey Bank failure.

When he went to the station expecting to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he was met instead by Anne and decided to bring her to Green Gables to let his sister Marilla handle the mistake. Matthew quietly advocated for keeping Anne and gave her simple delights, such as visiting her room to gently persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Lynde so she could stay, and gifting her a package of chocolate sweets. After Anne completed her studies at Queen's Academy, Matthew spent a tender final evening with her before dying suddenly from the shock of reading about the Abbey Bank failure.

value: Matthew Cuthbert said: “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat. “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself.”

label: Quote
value: Matthew Cuthbert said: “Well now, I can’t seem to,” said Matthew, as he opened the yard gate to let the cows through. “It’s only that I’m getting old, Anne, and keep forgetting it. Well, well, I’ve always worked pretty hard and I’d rather drop in harness.”

label: Quote
value: Matthew Cuthbert said: "I reckon she ought to be punished a little. But don’t be too hard on her, Marilla. Recollect she hasn’t ever had anyone to teach her right. You’re—you’re going to give her something to eat, aren’t you?"

label: Quote
value: Matthew Cuthbert said: "It’ll have to be done sooner or later, you know, for Marilla’s a dreadful determined woman—dreadful determined, Anne. Do it right off, I say, and have it over."

label: Quote
value: Matthew Cuthbert said: "That’s right—that’s right, Anne. But don’t tell Marilla I said anything about it. She might think I was putting my oar in and I promised not to do that."

label: Personality
value: Matthew is exceptionally shy.
unit: Matthew is an exceptionally shy, quiet, and reticent man who hates going among strangers and finds the prospect of meeting new people terrifying. Though non-confrontational and uninclined to argue or talk back, he possesses an incredible, silent persistency and holds fast to his opinions once set. He is a profoundly hardworking individual who does not seek out excitement and traditionally harbors a mortal dread of little girls. Despite his unobservant nature, he develops a strong desire to keep Anne at Green Gables and remains deeply admiring of her efforts.

label: History
value: Owen Ford was a magazine writer.
unit: Owen Ford was a magazine writer and newspaper man who was ordered to the sea by his doctor to recover from a bad spell of typhoid. As the grandson of schoolmaster John Selwyn, he arrived at Four Winds Harbor to board with Leslie Moore and aspired to write a great Canadian novel. Upon meeting Captain Jim, Owen became enthralled by the old sailor's memories and spent the summer writing a book based on Captain Jim's life-book. During his stay, Owen fell deeply in love with Leslie, but left the harbor in agony due to her marriage to Dick Moore. He later returned after learning Leslie was free, confessed his love to her in the garden, and sealed their commitment. Shortly after, Owen had his manuscript published and presented as a completed book to Captain Jim.

value: Owen Ford said: "Mrs. Blythe, this is a wonderful book—absolutely wonderful. If I could take it and use the material for a book I feel certain I could make the novel of the year out of it. Do you suppose Captain Jim would let me do it?"

value: Owen Ford said: “We’ll collaborate,” cried Owen delightedly. “You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work.”

label: Quote
value: Owen Ford said: “I have a good deal to do to it yet—revising and pruning and so forth,” he said, “but in the main it’s done. I wrote the last sentence this morning. If I can find a publisher for it it will probably be out next summer or fall.”

label: Quote
value: Owen Ford said: "Yes,—he’s mentally deficient, or something of the sort, isn’t he? But she said nothing about Mrs. Moore, and I supposed she’d be the usual hustling country housewife who takes in boarders to earn an honest penny."

value: Owen Ford said: "Oh, I won’t mind him. I don’t suppose I’ll be much in the house anyhow, except for meals. But what a shame it all is! Her life must be a hard one."

label: History
value: Paul Irving moved from the States to live with his grandmother
unit: Paul Irving moved from the States to live with his grandmother in Avonlea, three years after his mother passed away. He became a bright, imaginative pupil under schoolteacher Anne Shirley, quickly establishing himself as her favorite student by sharing his vivid compositions, letters, and tales of imaginary shore friends. Paul formed a close bond with Anne, visiting local cemeteries with her to place flowers on graves and joining her on visits to Echo Lodge. There, he connected deeply with Miss Lavendar over their shared imaginative nature. After Anne helped reunite Paul's father, Stephen Irving, with Miss Lavendar, Paul discussed their upcoming wedding and romantic future with Anne. Over time, Paul turned his creative thoughts into verse, becoming a published poet whose work appeared in magazines. Years later, he returned to Green Gables as a guest to celebrate the wedding of Anne and Gilbert Blythe.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon is a lively and wealthy student
unit: Philippa "Phil" Gordon, a lively and wealthy student from an exclusive family in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant while exploring Old St. John's Cemetery on their first day at Redmond College. The three quickly formed a close friendship, and after Anne and Priscilla arranged to rent a house called Patty's Place, Phil asked to join their household for the following school year. While living at Patty's Place, she frequently entertained various suitors, but her romantic path changed during a summer trip when she met Jonas Blake, a theological student. Deeply moved after hearing him preach, Phil fell in love with him and eventually accepted his proposal, prioritizing him over her other admirers. Throughout college, Phil remained a confidante to Anne, comforting and confronting her through various romantic dilemmas involving Gilbert Blythe and Roy Gardner. Following graduation, Phil married Jonas. Years later, she and her husband attended Anne's wedding at Green Gables, by which point Phil had become thin after having babies of her own.

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Heaps. The boys like me awfully—they really do. But there were only two that mattered. The rest were all too young and too poor. I must marry a rich man, you know."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "And let me come to see you. I want to be chummy with you. I’ve taken such a fancy to you both. And I haven’t quite disgusted you with my frivolity, have I?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I’ll go, if I can walk with Priscilla and Charlie. That will be a bearable degree of gooseberry. That Gilbert of yours is a darling, Anne, but why does he go around so much with Goggle-eyes?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I don’t want William’s Island especially, but I’m sure I couldn’t get it if I did. Look at that sentry on the summit of the fort, right beside the flag. Doesn’t he look as if he had stepped out of a romance?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Look—in white letters, around the archway over the gate. ‘Patty’s Place.’ Isn’t that killing? Especially on this Avenue of Pinehursts and Elmwolds and Cedarcrofts? ‘Patty’s Place,’ if you please! I adore it."

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips was a teacher
unit: Mr. Phillips was a teacher known for frequently whipping his students while failing to maintain any order in his classroom. During his time at the school, he disciplined Anne Shirley by making her stand in front of the class after she broke a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head, and later forced her to sit next to Gilbert as a further punishment. He eventually departed from his role as the local schoolmaster, leaving Anne emotional about his leaving as the community prepared to welcome a new minister and subsequent changes.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy with her close friend Anne Shirley. Following her schooling, she was hired to teach at Carmody school. Later, she served as a conduit for famous author Charlotte E. Morgan—who was Priscilla's aunt—arranging visits and bringing Mrs. Morgan to Green Gables to meet Anne. When Priscilla matriculated at Redmond College in Kingsport, she warmly greeted Anne at the train station and helped her adjust to university life. While strolling through Old St. John's Cemetery, Priscilla and Anne befriended fellow student Philippa Gordon. Seeking a new residence for their upcoming school year, Priscilla and Anne discovered that Patty's Place was available for rent and successfully secured the home alongside Stella Maynard and Aunt Jamesina. Over the course of their college years, Priscilla shared in the lively home life at Patty's Place, hosted summer visits in Avonlea, and ultimately completed her studies at Redmond through Convocation.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally hardworking woman
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally hardworking, capable, and practical woman who manages her own affairs alongside those of others. Known as a meddlesome gossip and a critical, outspoken observer, she prides herself on speaking her mind freely without fear or favor. Despite her sharp tongue, she possesses a deeply kind soul and is a gently skillful, tender, and unwearied nurse when tending to the sick. She is a passionate political enthusiast, loves being asked for advice, and compulsively tries to correct and properly raise anyone she lives with. Additionally, she harbors a distinct prejudice against Americans, strongly opposes higher education for women, and holds dubious views regarding the propriety of writing fiction.

value: Royal Gardner was a handsome Redmond student.
unit: Royal Gardner was a handsome Redmond student who had previously left college and gone abroad for two years due to his mother's failing health. He met Anne Shirley during a sudden rainstorm, rescuing her with his umbrella and walking her home before sending her a dozen roses. After escorting Anne to a reception and introducing his mother and sisters to her, Roy took her to the harbor pavilion upon their college graduation and proposed. However, Anne realized she did not love him and refused his offer, leaving Roy deeply upset as they parted ways.

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea as a classmate of Anne Shirley, having famously charmed away all her warts with a magic pebble as a child. A member of Anne's childhood story club, Ruby declared early on that she intended to have many suitors when she grew up. She attended school alongside Anne, eventually progressing with her to Queen's Academy to train as a teacher. Following their time at Queen's, Ruby gained a reputation for lively social chatter and flirtatious behavior back in Avonlea. However, she later fell terminally ill with consumption. Though she initially hid her failing health behind a façade of gaiety, Ruby eventually confided her deep fear of dying and her desire to live during an emotional evening with Anne. Shortly after that conversation, Ruby passed away peacefully in her sleep, leaving her friends to mourn her loss.

Following their time at Queen's, Ruby gained a reputation for lively social chatter and flirtatious behavior back in Avonlea. However, she later fell terminally ill with consumption. Though she initially hid her failing health behind a façade of gaiety, Ruby eventually confided her deep fear of dying and her desire to live during an emotional evening with Anne. Shortly after that conversation, Ruby passed away peacefully in her sleep, leaving her friends to mourn her loss.

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "It makes me feel frightened, girls. Do you suppose it’s really right to act like this? Mrs. Lynde says that all play-acting is abominably wicked."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I’ll try. I’ll think over what you have said, and try to believe it. And you’ll come up as often as you can, won’t you, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "There’s a concert at Carmody and a party at White Sands. Herb Spencer’s going to take me. He’s my latest. Be sure to come up tomorrow. I’m dying for a good talk with you. I want to hear all about your doings at Redmond."

label: History
value: Rusty was found thin.
unit: After being found thin, singed, and damaged, Rusty trotted close to Anne's heels as he followed her home, having recently fought and defeated the tobacco-king's cat. Anne reluctantly adopted the disreputable stray at Patty's Place, where he miraculously survived a chloroforming attempt and earned a permanent spot in the house. Upon Aunt Jamesina's arrival with her own pets, Rusty attempted to fight the newcomers, getting put in his place by the Sarah-cat while engaging in repeated battles with Joseph before eventually becoming his close friend. He later contributed to a chaotic scene at Patty's Place when Royal Gardner's mother and sisters made an unexpected visit.

label: History
value: Miss Sarah Copp lived at the Copp home on the Tory Road.
unit: Miss Sarah Copp lived at the Copp home on the Tory Road, where she had been forced by her sister Martha to whitewash an old duck house every spring. After Anne Shirley fell through the roof of the duck house while trying to look into the pantry, Sarah rescued her and later entertained Anne and Diana Wright over tea and bread, selling Anne a willow-ware platter and announcing her own upcoming marriage. Her father had previously sent away her suitor, Luther Wallace, twenty years earlier because he was poor. In addition, Aunt Jamesina possessed a pet named the Sarah-cat, who had been given to her by her washerwoman and who quickly put the stray cat Rusty in his place upon arriving at Patty's Place.

label: History
value: Stacy served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea.
unit: Miss Stacy served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea, maintaining order without ever whipping her pupils. Upon starting her tenure, she proposed organizing a Christmas concert to raise funds for a school flag, which her students eagerly embraced. At the end of her first term, she announced she would return the following year to prepare students for the Queen's Entrance examination, subsequently guiding them through their studies for the crucial tests. She eventually left Avonlea after accepting a position at a grade school in her home district.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant before spending time working as a schoolteacher. Looking ahead to her next year of college, she proposed renting a house with Anne and Priscilla, suggesting her Aunt Jamesina act as their housekeeper. The group, joined by Philippa Gordon, successfully secured Patty's Place and settled into a lively household together for the school year. During their time living at Patty's Place, Stella and her housemates balanced their Redmond examinations with household antics, social calls, and creative endeavors, including a rainy afternoon spent with Anne reading old melodramatic stories. As their college life drew to a close after graduation, Stella packed up her belongings alongside her friends as they prepared to part ways.

value: Susan said: "Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning."

label: Quote
value: Susan said: "If you cannot I will not go, Mrs. Doctor, dear, Matilda’s leg to the contrary notwithstanding. I will not have you worried, and that blessed child upset in consequence, for any number of legs."

label: Quote
value: Susan said: “Do not tell me,” said Susan fiercely, answering the anguish in Marilla’s eyes, “that God could be so cruel as to take that darling lamb from us when we all love her so much.”

value: Susan said: “Now for breakfast,” she said briskly. “I am of the opinion that we will all be glad of a bite and sup. You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.”

label: Quote
value: Susan said: "Oh, the poor lamb—the poor lamb! How can she bear it, Miss Cuthbert? I am afraid it will kill her. She has been that built up and happy, longing for that baby, and planning for it. Cannot anything be done nohow, Miss Cuthbert?"

label: Appearance
value: Uncle Jim is a tall man.
unit: Uncle Jim is a tall, rather ungainly man with a somewhat stooped figure that nevertheless suggests great strength and endurance. He has a deeply lined, bronzed, and clean-shaven face framed by a thick mane of hair falling to his shoulders. His remarkably blue, deep-set eyes are clear and steady, appearing to twinkle or dream. Over time, he shows signs of aging, coming to appear frail and bent with noticeably grayer hair and a slightly trembling hand.

label: Personality
value: Captain Jim is a high-souled man.
unit: Captain Jim is a high-souled, simple-minded man possessing a rare and fine soul, with eternal youth in his eyes and heart. Known for his placid demeanor and invariable cheerfulness, he admits to having formed a habit of enjoying things and is a passionate worshipper of beauty. He is philosophical by nature, preferring to ponder all kinds of problems even if he cannot solve them. A born storyteller with a knack for bringing far-off things vividly to life, he also possesses a tolerable skill at playing his old brown fiddle. His single expressed fear is the horror of a lingering death.

label: History
value: Captain Jim came from a line of sea-going people.
unit: Coming from a line of sea-going people, Captain Jim ran off to sea as a boy and spent a lifetime traveling the world, though his youth was marred when his sweetheart, Margaret, drowned at sea. Fifty years after her loss and five years after retiring from his life on the ocean, he lived at the Four Winds Point lighthouse with his cat, the First Mate. There he welcomed Anne and Gilbert Blythe to the community, quickly forming a close bond with Anne as a kindred spirit and introducing the couple to his collection of curios and true sea tales. Over the following months, Captain Jim frequently hosted Anne, Gilbert, and their neighbor Leslie Moore, offering comfort to Anne when she grieved the loss of her newborn daughter, Joyce, and entrusting her with the story of his lost Margaret. He also shared his written journal of sea adventures with the Blythes, which led to an introduction to visiting author Owen Ford. Owen borrowed the life-book and agreed to write Captain Jim's life story combined with the tale of Margaret, drafting the manuscript at the lighthouse over the course of the summer. Later, when Gilbert discovered a medical possibility regarding Leslie's husband, Captain Jim lent Leslie the money she needed to travel to Montreal for the procedure, and he was eventually honored when Anne and Gilbert named their newborn son, James Matthew, after him. Sometime after celebrating a Liberal political victory, Captain Jim had a poignant conversation with Anne at the lighthouse, confiding his belief that his death was near and asking her to care for the First Mate when he was gone. After offering a warm benediction to Leslie and Owen upon their engagement, Captain Jim was presented by Anne and Leslie with the newly published copy of his life-book. The following morning, Anne and Gilbert saw the lighthouse light still burning after sunrise and entered to find that Captain Jim had peacefully passed away in his sleep with his published book resting on his chest.

Fifty years after her loss and five years after retiring from his life on the ocean, he lived at the Four Winds Point lighthouse with his cat, the First Mate. There he welcomed Anne and Gilbert Blythe to the community, quickly forming a close bond with Anne as a kindred spirit and introducing the couple to his collection of curios and true sea tales. Over the following months, Captain Jim frequently hosted Anne, Gilbert, and their neighbor Leslie Moore, offering comfort to Anne when she grieved the loss of her newborn daughter, Joyce, and entrusting her with the story of his lost Margaret. He also shared his written journal of sea adventures with the Blythes, which led to an introduction to visiting author Owen Ford. Owen borrowed the life-book and agreed to write Captain Jim's life story combined with the tale of Margaret, drafting the manuscript at the lighthouse over the course of the summer. Later, when Gilbert discovered a medical possibility regarding Leslie's husband, Captain Jim lent Leslie the money she needed to travel to Montreal for the procedure, and he was eventually honored when Anne and Gilbert named their newborn son, James Matthew, after him. Sometime after celebrating a Liberal political victory, Captain Jim had a poignant conversation with Anne at the lighthouse, confiding his belief that his death was near and asking her to care for the First Mate when he was gone. After offering a warm benediction to Leslie and Owen upon their engagement, Captain Jim was presented by Anne and Leslie with the newly published copy of his life-book. The following morning, Anne and Gilbert saw the lighthouse light still burning after sunrise and entered to find that Captain Jim had peacefully passed away in his sleep with his published book resting on his chest.

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "The Government don’t give lighthouse keepers such luxuries. Look at the colors that wood makes. If you’d like some driftwood for your fire, Mistress Blythe, I’ll bring you up a load some day. Sit down. I’m going to make you a cup of tea."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "That’s Marshall Elliott—a mighty fine man with jest one streak of foolishness in him. I s’pose you wondered what his object was in turning himself into a sort of dime museum freak."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "Come, now, Cornelia, I can’t see any harm in going to the Methodist church when there’s no preaching in your own. I’ve been a Presbyterian for seventy-six years, and it isn’t likely my theology will hoist anchor at this late day."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "I wanted to hear some good singing. The Methodists have a good choir; and you can’t deny, Cornelia, that the singing in our church is awful since the split in the choir."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "That’s just exactly the truth about Lewis Taylor. When I see those poor, miserable children of his, robbed of all children ought to have, it p’isens my own bite and sup for days afterwards."

value: Walter is the father of Anne.
unit: Walter was the father of Anne, who died of fever alongside his wife, Bertha, when Anne was only three months old. His death left Anne an orphan, forcing her into a childhood of moving between families and caring for children before being sent to an asylum. Years later, Anne visited Walter's former home in Bolingbroke and his grave, where she received and read a packet of old love letters written between Walter and Bertha, finally allowing her to feel deeply connected to her parents.

value: Anne begins her first day teaching school.
chapter: v2 · V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am
unit: Anne begins her first day teaching school, forgetting her prepared speech but managing her new pupils, including the sullen Anthony Pye and a bright, imaginative boy named Paul Irving. After school, an excessively dressed Mrs. Donnell visits to demand specific pronunciations and names for her children. On her walk home, Paul gives Anne wild orchids, brightening her mood before she returns to recount her day to Marilla Cuthbert and Rachel Lynde.

value: Anne bids a tearful farewell to her home at Green Gables.
chapter: v3 · Chapter III Greeting and Farewell
unit: Anne bids a tearful farewell to her home at Green Gables and leaves for Redmond College with Gilbert and Charlie Sloane. After a rainy drive to the station and a boat ride from Charlottetown, she and Gilbert travel by train to Kingsport. Upon arrival, Anne is warmly met by Priscilla Grant, who takes her by cab to their new boardinghouse while cheering her up.

unit: Anne, Priscilla, and Phil Gordon go for an afternoon walk with Gilbert and Charlie Sloane through the park and along the harbor shore. label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER V. Anne’s History
unit: During the drive to White Sands, Anne resolves to enjoy the journey despite her dread of being sent away. unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. unit: Anne joins Marilla, Mrs. Rachel, Dora, and Davy outside on a June evening. Davy complains about his schoolwork and the local funerals, but Anne offers to help him with his arithmetic. Anne later wanders down to Dryad's Bubble, feeling melancholic about Gilbert's absence and the changes that growing up brings.

Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

unit: Anne and Diana visit Echo Lodge to help Charlotta the Fourth and Miss Lavendar prepare for the upcoming wedding. The next day, Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving are married in the garden in front of their guests, after which everyone sees them off at the station. While locking up the stone house afterward, Anne and Gilbert share a quiet, poignant moment that subtly alters the nature of their relationship as they look toward their college years.

chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: Suffering from a severe toothache, Anne has a disastrous and irritable day at school, accidentally throwing a package of fireworks into the stove and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

label: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
value: Davy questions Anne about sleep.
chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: Davy questions Anne about sleep and Marilla's frugality before Marilla calls Anne over to see Diana's signal. Diana tells Anne about a willow-ware platter at the Copp home on the Tory Road, which they decide to retrieve the following day. When they arrive at the empty Copp house, Anne climbs onto an old duck house to look through the pantry window, falls through the roof, and gets trapped. After sitting through a rainstorm while stuck, Anne is rescued by Miss Sarah Copp, who agrees to entertain selling her the platter over tea.

At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. At church on Sunday, Davy creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down Lauretta White's neck during the service. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

unit: Suffering from a severe toothache, Anne has a disastrous and irritable day at school, accidentally throwing a package of fireworks into the stove and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. She returns home distraught over losing her temper, but Marilla comforts her. The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

unit: Anne returns to Avonlea for a snowbound and lonely Christmas vacation, feeling embarrassed by Gilbert's romantic attentions and worried about her finances for her next year at Redmond. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. At church on Sunday, Davy creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down Lauretta White's neck during the service. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

chapter: v3 · Chapter VIII Anne’s First Proposal
unit: During an overnight stay, Jane Andrews proposes to Anne on behalf of her shy brother, Billy. To cap off the disastrous day, Miss Barry's expensive platter is accidentally smashed, and Anne later receives a letter explaining Mrs. Morgan injured her ankle.

unit: Janet takes Anne to a prayer meeting in Valley Road, where they meet John Douglas, who walks Janet home. value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

chapter: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women
unit: Anne and Diana travel along the Newbridge road to collect subscriptions for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society to repaint the local hall. They encounter pessimistic Miss Eliza Andrews, who refuses to give anything, though her sister Catherine secretly donates afterwards. Later, Anne recounts to Marilla how they helped flustered Dan Blair mix a cake in exchange for a generous donation, followed by their visit to meticulous Mrs. Theodore White.

value: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora.
chapter: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
unit: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora, leaving Anne to do household chores while Davy goes to help Mr. Harrison. While transferring bed feathers, Anne mistakenly applies rug dye to her nose instead of freckle lotion, turning it bright red just before Priscilla Grant arrives with famous author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. Diana helps Anne wash off the dye and supplies a roast chicken, allowing Anne to successfully entertain her visitors with a lovely dinner and a walk through the surrounding woods.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

value: Anne returns to Avonlea.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XI The Round of Life
unit: Upon returning to Avonlea, Anne notices small changes in the community and learns from Rachel Lynde that Ruby Gillis is terminally ill with consumption. On their way to visit Ruby, Anne and Diana stop by to leave jelly with the sour and critical Aunt Atossa. Anne confides in Diana her ambition to write a short story before they arrive at the lively Gillis home, where Ruby hides her failing health under a façade of gay flirtation.

unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

She enjoys weekend visits home to Avonlea during the autumn and spends spare time visiting Miss Barry at Beechwood. As spring arrives and final exams loom, Anne and her friends gather to discuss their anxieties, upcoming commencement clothes, and hopes for the future.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road
value: Marilla returns from the oculist.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road
unit: Marilla returns from the oculist with news that her failing sight means she cannot read, sew, or manage Green Gables alone, forcing her to consider selling the farm. Anne refuses to let the home be sold and decides to give up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally. Later, Mrs. Lynde informs them that Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea teaching position so Anne could have it, leading Anne to reconcile with Gilbert and look forward to her future with peace and hope.

chapter: v2 · IV Different Opinions
unit: On the evening before school opens, Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate their teaching methods and views on corporal punishment at a crossroads. Anne then walks back through her favorite spots, avoids Mrs. Lynde's unsolicited advice at Green Gables, and visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule without whipping. The next morning, a nervous Anne is comforted by Marilla as she prepares for her first day as a teacher.

value: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. Later, Mrs. Lynde discovers that Joshua Pye has accidentally painted the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up in color codes. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

unit: Marilla gives Anne permission to invite Diana over for tea while Marilla attends a meeting in Carmody. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.
